meta.title: Microsoft Fake Sign-In Sites Catalog
meta.purpose: Defensive threat-intel reference of URLs and techniques used to impersonate Microsoft sign-in pages (Microsoft 365, Outlook, Azure AD / Entra ID, Live) for detection engineering, blocklisting and threat hunting.
meta.warning: All URLs are DEFANGED malicious/illustrative samples for DETECTION ONLY. Do not visit or submit credentials. URLs neutralised (hxxp, [.]). Generic sample hosts are placeholders; the tracker replaces them with real observed indicators.

entries.technique: AiTM reverse-proxy phishing (Evilginx / Tycoon 2FA / EvilProxy) — the fake page proxies the real login.microsoftonline.com in real time to steal the session cookie and defeat MFA.
entries.detection: Sign-ins where the client/redirect host is NOT login.microsoftonline.com but the auth flow completes; new session from an unusual ASN immediately after a phishing click; Entra ID risky sign-in + token replay from a different IP within minutes.
entries.source: Microsoft Threat Intelligence — AiTM / Tycoon 2FA reporting
entries.notes: Cloudflare Workers (.workers.dev) and pages.dev commonly abused as disposable hosting.

entries.technique: Fake Microsoft login kit dropped on a compromised legitimate CMS (WordPress) under /wp-content or /wp-includes; credentials POSTed to an attacker collector or Telegram bot.
entries.detection: Outbound POST to /wp-content|/wp-includes paths containing office365/login/verify; referer chain from webmail; hunt proxy logs for '*/wp-content/*login*.php'.
entries.notes: Legit domain reputation helps the URL bypass mail filters.

entries.technique: Email-prefill phishing — the victim address is placed after '#' so the fake page auto-fills the username and renders the corporate tenant branding, increasing credibility.
entries.detection: URL fragment (#) containing a full email address; page that mirrors tenant branding on a non-Microsoft host; hunt for URLs with '#'+ email pattern in web logs.
entries.notes: Common in Mamba 2FA / Greatness / Caffeine PhaaS kits.

entries.technique: Open-redirect / trusted-service abuse — the visible part of the URL references a legitimate Microsoft/third-party domain while the actual landing host is attacker-controlled.
entries.detection: URLs where a Microsoft-looking token appears in the query/path but the registrable domain is untrusted; open-redirect parameters (redir=, url=, next=) pointing off-domain.
entries.notes: Also abuses Google/LinkedIn/Baidu open redirects as the first hop.

entries.technique: Look-alike / typosquat domain (extra letter, hyphenation, TLD swap such as .com/.co/.online) hosting a static clone of the Microsoft sign-in page.
entries.detection: Newly-registered domains with edit-distance 1-2 to microsoftonline.com / office.com / login.live.com; homoglyph checks; Levenshtein/keyword hunting on NRD feeds.
entries.notes: Watch keywords: microsoft, msonline, office365, login, sso, mfa, secure, verify.

entries.technique: CAPTCHA-gated phishing — a Cloudflare Turnstile / hCaptcha / fake human-check is placed in front of the fake MS login to block crawlers and automated sandboxes before serving the credential form.
entries.detection: Phishing hosts that serve a challenge page to scanners but the real login form to browsers; hunt for turnstile/hcaptcha assets on non-Microsoft hosts that redirect to Microsoft-branded forms.

entries.technique: Quishing (QR-code phishing) — a PDF/image email embeds a QR code pointing to a fake Microsoft MFA/sign-in page, moving the click to a mobile device outside corporate controls.
entries.detection: Inbound mail with QR images and little text; endpoint/MDM telemetry showing mobile navigation to a Microsoft-branded non-Microsoft host shortly after mail delivery.
entries.notes: Often 'review the encrypted/secure document' or 'MFA re-enrollment' lures.

entries.url: hxxps://<attacker>[.]pages[.]dev/ (loads a local data:/blob: fake login)
entries.technique: HTML-attachment / blob-URL phishing — an .htm attachment or a page builds the fake Microsoft login entirely from an encoded (base64/blob:) blob rendered locally, so the credential form never appears as a fetched remote page.
entries.detection: Mail attachments (.htm/.html/.svg) that decode base64 into a login form; browser navigations to blob:/data: URIs presenting Microsoft branding; POST of credentials to a remote collector from a locally-rendered page.
entries.notes: Cloudflare Pages (.pages.dev), Netlify, Firebase and IPFS gateways abused as hosting.
